creator.name: Unknown painters of the Nordeste tradition

object.description: A red deer-like animal and small human figures on a sandstone shelter in the Serra da Capivara, where more than a thousand painted shelters record hunting, dancing and sex in the lively Nordeste style. The park is at the centre of the argument over when people reached the Americas: its excavator Niède Guidon claims hearths over 30,000 years old, far older than most archaeologists accept.
facts: Serra da Capivara holds the largest concentration of rock art in the Americas.
The Nordeste tradition is usually dated between about 12,000 and 6,000 years ago.
Capivara means capybara, the park's name animal.
